messages:
max: Quick FYI — I'm landing a small Terraform change for the ml-ingest service so it can write encrypted snapshots to the central-logs account KMS key. Can someone sanity-check the KMS grant + IRSA trust snippet? Trying to avoid the usual annotation/helm race we hit last quarter.

max: TL;DR of approach: create aws_iam_role for IRSA -> grant on cross-account KMS key via aws_kms_grant in logs acct. Using condition on sts:TagKeys/session and kms:GrantIsForAWSResource to limit scope. Snippets below.

max: Terraform IAM role (in ml account):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "ml_ingest_irsa" {
  name = "ml-ingest-irsa-role-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Principal = { Federated = var.oidc_provider_arn }
      Action = "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"
      Condition = { StringEquals = { "${var.oidc_provider_url}:sub" = "system:serviceaccount:ml:ingest-sa" } }
    }]
  })
}
```

max: KMS grant (in logs account):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "ml_ingest_grant" {
  name = "ml-ingest-grant-${var.env}"
  key_id = var.central_logs_kms_key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.ml_ingest_irsa.arn # created via remote state / data lookup
  operations = ["Encrypt","Decrypt","GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = { "service" = "ml-ingest" }
  }
}
```

max: KMS key policy still allows account principals; grant is used so we don't need to modify the key policy across accounts.

sam: Couple quick notes: 1) grantee_principal must be an IAM principal in the same account as the KMS key for aws_kms_grant to succeed unless you're using cross-account grants — double-check remote state wiring. 2) If the role ARN is passed from other account, make sure terraform provider credentials have kms:CreateGrant permission in logs acct.

anya: Also watch the session tags/conditions. We had an incident where the service minted sessions without the expected tags and the grant matched on encryption_context_subset failed. If you're going to guard on encryption_context, ensure the application sets the same context when calling GenerateDataKey.

luis: Re: IRSA trust snippet — looks fine but please ensure the exact OIDC issuer URL is used as in the cluster's OIDC provider (no trailing slash). Small mismatch there caused us issues before.

max: Good points. One more infra gotcha: Helm chart currently creates the serviceaccount as part of the release which sometimes means the annotation (eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn) gets applied after the pod starts -> race with csi-secret-store sidecar. Anyone remember the best fix?

anya: We patched by creating the SA separately via a kustomize pre-apply job for that chart. Alternatively, set serviceAccount.create=false in the chart and apply a standalone SA manifest first. Both work.

sam: If you want to keep helm ownership, another option is the helm post-renderer to inject the annotation earlier, but IMO simpler to manage SA outside helm for infra-critical SAs.

devops: infra-bot noticed a related TF plan in the PR — @max make sure the cross-account provider alias is used when creating the grant so it runs in logs acct context. Example: provider "aws" { alias = "logs" region = var.logs_region } then resource aws_kms_grant with provider = aws.logs.

max: Yep using provider alias. PR includes a tf remote-state data lookup for the logs KMS key id and a provider alias for logs acct.

luis: One more nit: for reproducibility, prefer aws_kms_grant only for short-lived grants and use key policy changes for long-term access. Grants can be revoked but if your app relies on it long-term, consider adding a key policy statement that allows the ML role principal (ARN pattern) from the ml account.

max: Good call — in this case we expect this to be long-lived (snapshot writes ongoing) so I'll open a follow-up with key-policy addition in logs account (with tight principal conditions) instead of an ephemeral grant. For now landing the grant to unblock staging.

anya: Sounds good. If you add the key-policy, include a condition on kms:EncryptionContext:service = "ml-ingest" and the principal ARN to minimize blast radius.

max: Will do. Action items: 1) I'll update PR to ensure provider alias for logs is set, 2) add explicit note for the app to include encryption_context when calling GenerateDataKey, 3) follow up with key-policy change ticket for prod.

sam: lgtm. @max please tag me on the PR, I'll do a quick review. :+1:

infra-bot: terraform plan completed for PR #428 — no permission errors in staging when running with logs provider alias.

max: Thanks all — landing the grant now and will open key-policy PR for prod next week.
